headline: Northeast states sue over $1.4 billion offshore-wind lease buyouts
dek: Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New York, Rhode Island and Vermont joined lawsuits challenging federal payments to cancel four planned projects.
body: A coalition of eight states filed two federal lawsuits Tuesday seeking to block agreements that would pay energy companies $1.4 billion to cancel four offshore-wind leases, including projects tied to the Northeast power grid.

The Rhode Island attorney general’s office said the cases challenge separate deals with Bluepoint Wind and Invenergy. The Bluepoint agreement covers a lease off New York and New Jersey; the Invenergy agreement covers three leases, including two in the Gulf of Maine.

Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island and Vermont are plaintiffs. The states argue that the Interior Department used federal settlement funds unlawfully and undermined state plans to add electricity capacity and reduce emissions.

The states’ filing says the canceled projects were expected to generate enough electricity for more than four million homes. The agreements would direct the companies toward other energy investments, while the lawsuits ask courts to set the deals aside under federal administrative and environmental laws.
The cases add to a series of state challenges to the administration’s offshore-wind policy. No court has yet ruled on the merits of the new claims.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Northeast states challenge offshore-wind lease buyouts
seoDescription: Eight states, including six in New England, sued over $1.4 billion in federal deals canceling four offshore-wind leases.
